messages:
mira: Quick sync — we need a decision on burst-credit sizing for reserved pools before Tuesday's roadmap review. Customers keep asking for predictable burst behavior but we also need to protect other tenants. Proposing a default of 2x baseline for burst credits that decays over a 30m ramp window. Thoughts?

alex: 2x seems reasonable as a starting point. Can we pin it to committed qps/GPUs instead of token rate? that maps better to infra.

dan: Agree on mapping to commit size. Also we need a hard-preempt threshold to avoid noisy-neighbor impact. Suggest preempt at 4x instantaneous usage with soft notifications.

pat: From finance — 2x default ok, but we should surface cost delta to the tenant when they enable burst. A simple per-minute burn estimate in console would help.

julie: Ops note: decay/ramp window should be configurable per-pool. Some enterprise customers will want shorter windows for latency-sensitive traffic.

mira: Good points. Updated straw proposal: default burst = 2x commit (by GPU slot), ramp decay = 30m, hard-preempt @4x instantaneous, pool-level override allowed. Also add visibility in console + cost estimator.

alex: Implementation questions for runtime: do we charge tokens or bill by GPU-minute? We already meter tokens for hosted. For Dedicated the commit is in GPU slots, so billing by GPU-minute for burst makes sense.

dan: Runtime needs an eviction signal. Prototype policy:

```
policy: {
  pool_match: "reserved:standard",
  burst_factor: 2.0,
  ramp_window_minutes: 30,
  hard_preempt_factor: 4.0,
  notify_tenant_at: [2.0, 3.0] // soft alerts
}
```

We can add `per_pool.override` later.

pat: Pricing team asks for a simple formula to show customers. Something like: "burst_cost_per_min = gpu_unit_price * active_burst_slots" — is that accurate?

alex: Yes for Dedicated. For hosted we continue token billing. We'll need a conversion estimate (tokens -> GPU-min) for the cost estimator. We can use p95 tokens/sec sample for the model family.

julie: SLO implications: if we allow 2x burst, what do we guarantee for baseline latency for non-burst tenants? We need a simulation to ensure p99 doesn't regress.

mira: Action items: 1) Eng (alex + dan) to prototype policy and simulate noisy-neighbor impact by EOD Thu. 2) Finance (pat) to draft burst pricing formula and a sample estimator by Fri. 3) Product (mira + julie) to write launch criteria and console mockup (canary gating + docs) by Mon. 4) Ops to add per-pool override and audit log requirement.

alex: I'll push a prototype branch. tentative config file we'll expose:

```
reserved_pools:
  - name: standard-committed
    commit_slots: 4
    burst:
      enabled: true
      factor: 2.0
      ramp_minutes: 30
      hard_preempt_factor: 4.0
```

Expect perf tests to show the eviction path works.

dan: For the simulation, I'll run traces from customers A/B to estimate cross-pool impact. If p99 regression > 10% we back off to 1.5x.

pat: Finance will also list three billing presentation options for the console: (a) GPU-min, (b) estimated token-equivalent, (c) blended view. Will share by Fri.

julie: Launch gating checklist suggestion:
- Canary with 1 customer on dedicated pool (2 weeks)
- No p99 latency regressions > 10% for other tenants
- Cost-estimator in Console + docs
- Fail-open fallback to lower-priority model variant
- Audit logs + tenant notifications

mira: Love the checklist. One more thing: for legal / contracts we need a clause for burst overages and support level. I'll loop in PL.

ops-bot: deploy:scheduled: Daily perf cluster run queued for 2026-03-22 03:00 UTC — will include burst-sim tests.

alex: Quick question — should we allow absolute caps (e.g., max_slots) per pool so enterprise customers can limit spend?

pat: Yes please — customers asked for a hard cap. UX should show projected spend at cap.

mira: Decision summary: default 2x by GPU-slot, ramp 30m, hard-preempt 4x, per-pool overrides + max_slots, show cost estimator in console. Consensus unless objections by EOD tomorrow. I'll capture and add to roadmap deck. :white_check_mark:
